evidence.reason: The test test_post_boundary_activation_refusal_is_required sets both post-boundary activation refusals to "success" simultaneously: manager_restart.after_phase.direct.rc = 0 (line 1885) and reboot.after_phase.dependency.rc = 0 (line 1890), then asserts only checks["mask_persisted"] is False (line 1895). Because mask_persisted is derived from both boundaries, a validator that inspects only the manager-restart boundary (direct.rc=0 → False) or only the reboot boundary (dependency.rc=0 → False) still computes False and the test passes. The test therefore cannot detect a validator that ignores either boundary, and it does not verify that each refusal result independently contributes to the check. Starting from valid refusals and flipping one boundary at a time would make each case discriminating. This is a test-correctness defect (false confidence) in existing behavior, not a contract-scope enlargement.
